samples.summary: Hyperlink runs are a second place where an explicit `false` carries information, and `styleOffAsClear` does not exempt it — toggling underline off on a link is now a visual no-op.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:387-391 renders `let showUnderline = style.underline ?? false; if (style.href) { ... if (style.underline === undefined) showUnderline = true; }`. So for a run with `href`, an ABSENT `underline` key means "paint the link default underline", and only an explicit `underline: false` suppresses it. `Doc.styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:398-417) preserves `false` only when the block's *named-style* defaults set the key (`resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), ...)`); a hyperlink in a normal paragraph has no named-style underline, so the `false` is demoted to `undefined`. Result: selecting a link and toggling underline off (Cmd+U / toolbar U, whose write funnels through `Doc.applyInlineStyle`) now clears the key and paint-layout immediately re-applies the link's default underline — the user can no longer remove a link's underline, and the raw-style-based `getRangeStyleSummary` will report underline OFF while the canvas paints it ON (the exact toolbar/render disagreement issue #715 was about). The fix belongs on the new code: the exemption in `styleOffAsClear` needs to also keep `false` for `underline` when the slice being written carries `href` (or the paint default has to move into the resolved-style layer).

samples.summary: The demotion is enforced only in `Doc`; `DocStore.applyStyle`/`applyStyles` are public and are called directly by the editors, so the "never store a dead boolean flag" invariant has an open bypass.
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` is applied only at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:377 and :431. Two live call sites write inline style straight to the store, skipping it: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1095 (`docStore.applyStyles(...)`, font-size stepping) and packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:907 (same for the text-box editor). Today both only pass `{ fontSize }`, so no boolean reaches them and nothing is broken right now — but `DocStore.applyStyle` (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:76) and `applyStyles` (:90) are the documented write API and remain reachable with `bold: false`, as packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1328 (`expect(result.inlines[0].style.bold).toBe(false)`) demonstrates for the Yorkie store path. Consider documenting on `DocStore.applyStyle` that boolean-off must arrive as `undefined`, or moving the demotion into the store helper so every entry point passes through it.

samples.summary: No normalization/migration for documents that already persisted `false` flags, so the dead-flag and lazy-cascade symptoms survive on existing content and a newly cleared run still cannot merge with a legacy `false` neighbour.
samples.evidence: `inlineStylesEqual` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:418 area) compares strictly, so a legacy run carrying `italic: false` never merges with a neighbour that now simply lacks the key, and it still will not follow a Heading style later redefined to be italic — the exact hazard the change is fixing, left in place for every already-saved document. Nothing in the diff or in the load path (`MemDocStore.setDocument`, `YorkieDocStore.parseInlineStyle` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:168-173, `Doc.refresh` → `normalizeInlinesArray` at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:805) demotes a stored `false`. The task file docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md:60-66 lists Yorkie tree-node merging as a non-goal but does not mention existing stored flags at all.
searchedFor: grep for 'migrat' style normalization on load (none found)

samples.summary: `removedInlineStyleAttrs` is fed the pre-mutual-exclusion style, so the super/subscript exclusion clear never reaches the CRDT — now that the model-side merge truly deletes the key, cache and tree disagree instead of merely differing in representation.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:337-343 injects `resolvedStyle.subscript = undefined` (mutual exclusion) *inside* the helper, and after this change `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325) deletes that key from the cached run. The Yorkie store, however, computes both `serializeInlineStyle(style)` and `removedInlineStyleAttrs(style)` from the caller's original `style` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1882-1883), which does not contain the injected `subscript: undefined`, so no `removeStyleByPath` is emitted and `subscript="true"` survives on the Tree node while the cache no longer has the key. Pre-existing in kind, but the diff sharpens it into a cache/tree mismatch that reappears on the next dirty re-parse.

samples.summary: `styleOffAsClear` adds a `findBlock` lookup per written block slice on the hottest editing path; for a cell rectangle toggle-off that is one lookup per cell block, each of which can fall back to a full recursive table walk.
samples.evidence: `this.findBlock(blockId)` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:176-186 → `findBlockInCells` at :192-219) uses the layout-time `_blockParentMap` as a fast path but falls back to `walkCellsForBlock` over body + header + footer for any block not yet in the map. `applyInlineStyleToCellRectangle` (document.ts:431) invokes `styleOffAsClear` once per visited cell block, so a bold-off over a large rectangle whose parent map is stale becomes O(cells × document walk).

verdict.reason: Verified independently. paint-layout.ts:387-391 does treat an ABSENT `underline` on an `href` run as "paint the link default underline", so only an explicit `underline: false` suppresses it. `Doc.styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:399-418) rewrites an explicit `false` to `undefined` for every key in BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS (includes 'underline', document.ts:42) and exempts only keys supplied by the block's named style (line 410/413) — a hyperlink in a normal paragraph has no such default, so the `false` is demoted. The demotion physically deletes the key (mergeInlineStyle, block-helpers.ts:316-325, used by applyInlineStyle at block-helpers.ts:367), and both write funnels go through styleOffAsClear (document.ts:377, 431). Reachable via Cmd+U (text-editor.ts:887 → toggleStyle 2886-2903 → applyStyleToSelection → doc.applyInlineStyle 2935) and the toolbar (editor.ts:1031); since the toggle derives the boolean from the runs, the stored state cycles true → cleared → true and a link's underline can never be removed, while getRangeStyleSummary (editor.ts:2644-2714) reads the raw style and would report underline off — the toolbar/render disagreement the surrounding comments say issue #715 was about. No guard elsewhere exempts href runs, and no test covers it (no `underline: false` occurrence in packages/docs; document.test.ts:648-673 covers href only). In-lane for blast radius: an out-of-diff consumer relies on the `false` vs absent invariant that the new clearing behaviour breaks; major impact.

finding.summary: Format painter (Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V) silently loses its ability to REMOVE B/I/U/S now that toggle-off clears the key instead of storing `false`
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:869 captures the painter buffer as the RAW caret run style (`this.styleBuffer = { ...this.getStyleAtCursor() }`, and `getStyleAtCursor` is documented at :2942-2949 as raw run style), and :1013 applies it via `applyStyleToSelection(range, this.styleBuffer)` → `Doc.applyInlineStyle` → `mergeInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:316-325), which only merges keys that are PRESENT in the patch. Before this PR a run that the user had un-bolded carried an explicit `bold: false`, so copying its formatting onto bold text un-bolded it. With `styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:399-418) the key is deleted from the run, so the painter buffer no longer contains `bold`/`italic`/`underline`/`strikethrough` at all and pasting the format onto bold/italic target text leaves the target's formatting in place. Neither call site was updated to compensate (e.g. by materialising explicit `false`/`undefined` for the boolean keyset when capturing). Fix belongs at the painter capture site, or by having the painter capture the full boolean keyset.

finding.summary: Toggle-off now emits a Yorkie `removeStyleByPath` op on the hottest editing path (B/I/U/S); if Yorkie history cannot reverse TreeStyleRemove, Cmd+Z after a toggle-off silently stops restoring the flag
finding.evidence: With the demotion in `Doc.styleOffAsClear`, every B/I/U/S off-toggle now reaches `YorkieDocStore.applyStyleInTree` with the key set to `undefined`, so `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) returns the attr and `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` runs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1881 — previously only `styleByPath` ran for a toggle-off (the `false` was serialized), and `removeStyleByPath` was reached only by the rare removeLink / clear-formatting paths. Docs undo is Yorkie-history based (`this.doc.history.undo()` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2611), so the reversibility of the removeStyle op is now load-bearing for the most common formatting action in the product. I could not verify the SDK's reverse-op support from this checkout (the Yorkie SDK is not installed in node_modules here); confirming needs a collab/integration run that toggles bold off and then undoes it against a real Yorkie doc. Fix, if real, belongs in the Yorkie store (emit a compensating style write) rather than in the new Doc code.
